source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Fairly few specific precautions actually being needed once a fistula is considered healthy and fully well established","B":"Avoiding blood pressure measurements, venipuncture, and IV access on the fistula arm, and monitoring for signs of infection or malfunction","C":"Restricting all movement of the fistula arm permanently, regardless of how well the fistula is actually functioning over time","D":"Allowing blood pressure measurements and IV access to be performed on the fistula arm just as they would on any other arm"}}
source_row.rationale: AV fistula care teaching includes avoiding blood pressure measurements, venipuncture, and IV access on the fistula arm (to protect this vital access), and monitoring for signs of infection or malfunction (such as loss of thrill or bruit), essential for maintaining long-term access viability.
